title: How the Solar System Formed
objective: After this level you can outline how the Sun and planets formed from a collapsing cloud of gas and dust.
summary: A collapsing, spinning cloud flattened into a disk: the Sun at its center, rocky planets inside the frost line, giants outside.

cards.headline: Every planet, moon and comet began as part of one cloud.
A spinning cloud collapses
cards.body: About 4.6 billion years ago, a cloud of gas and dust began collapsing under its own gravity. As it shrank it spun faster and flattened into a disk, with the young Sun forming at the center. That’s why the planets still orbit in nearly the same plane.

cards.headline: The frost line
cards.body: Close to the young Sun it was too hot for ices to form, so only rock and metal could clump into planets: small, rocky worlds. Farther out, beyond the frost line, ices could condense too. With far more material to build from, the giant planets grew huge.

cards.headline: Origins: reconstructed
learned: The solar system formed ~4.6 billion years ago
A spinning cloud collapsed into a flat disk
Inside the frost line, rocky planets formed
Outside it, ices helped the giants grow

questions.prompt: What did the solar system form from?

options.label: A piece of an older sun that broke off
options.rationale: The solar system formed from a cloud.

options.label: A collapsing cloud of gas and dust
Rocks captured from other stars
options.rationale: It formed from its own cloud.

questions.explanation: About 4.6 billion years ago, a cloud of gas and dust collapsed under gravity to form the Sun and planets.

questions.prompt: Why are the inner planets rocky and the outer planets giants?

options.label: The giants formed first and later moved outward
options.rationale: The frost line explains the pattern.

options.label: The Sun pushed all the gas outward
options.rationale: Ices condensing far out is the key.

options.label: Beyond the frost line, ices could form too, giving giants more to build with
Rocky planets are just giants that lost their gas
options.rationale: They formed rocky from the start.

questions.explanation: Near the Sun only rock and metal could condense. Farther out, ices could too, so the outer planets had much more material and grew into giants.

questions.prompt: From Level 15: the planets all lie near the ecliptic. What does the formation story say about why?

options.label: The planets were captured into that plane later
The Sun’s magnetic field lines them up
The stars pull them into a line
options.rationale: Distant stars don’t shape the orbits.

options.label: They formed from one flat, spinning disk

questions.explanation: The collapsing cloud flattened into a spinning disk, so the planets formed, and still orbit, in nearly one plane: the ecliptic.
